title: Olympus Mons is nearly three Everests, and gently sloped
body: Mars's shield volcano Olympus Mons rises about 22 kilometres above datum, roughly two and a half times Everest's height, yet its flanks slope only a few degrees, so a hiker might barely notice the climb. Low gravity and a stationary crust let lava pile in one place for eons. It is a mountain the size of a country with the manners of a ramp.
